title: THE STAR THAT ONLY SPOKE IN FLARES
deck: A ring habitat of fourteen thousand has seventy hours to decide whether its star is attacking it, and the only evidence that it is not is a silence nobody had thought to measure.
shape: Six scenes across four days: a council's case for flight, a physicist's nine-year ledger and the lever hidden in it, a vote taken on terms the council wrote, two moved gaps that do not answer cleanly, a decision altered by its dissenters, and a dawn when a whole ring goes quiet and the star answers in a shape no one can read yet.

scenes.title: Seventy Hours
paragraphs: *Calloway Reach, Ring Council chamber · Day 1, 06:10*

The clock on the chamber wall read 70:00:00. Someone had put it there so that it would be read aloud, and nobody had. Outside the long window the ring turned slowly under a red sun the size of a coin, with fourteen thousand people on its inner face, and the room smelled of cold tea and of a council that had not slept.

Illuminara had come aboard three weeks earlier on an ice tender, hired by the Rakel cooperative to model how heat and light loaded the cutting quays. She was in the chamber because her models were the only ones nobody had yet argued with. She stood at the back, beside the water jug.

**Teodora Vance**  
The Wick has thrown six dangerous bursts in eleven days. In nine years of records it threw about one a month. Eleven days is two hundred and sixty-four hours; six bursts in that time is one every forty-four, and that is not a fluctuation I can fold into the background. They cluster after our evening traffic peaks. The next natural alignment is due at about four in the morning on Day Four. Under ordinary traffic the shield office forecasts one point three times the rating of our parasol. Ferries need twenty-six hours to finish loading, and I will not cut a two-hour margin out of a ring's lives. The order has to go out by hour forty-two.

**Pell Rourke**  
The parasol takes one burst. I will not promise it takes that one.

**Illuminara**  
What does leaving cost?

**Teodora Vance**  
Rakel. Everything we mine. A ring that leaves carries eight months of water, and after that it's a very large cup.
Vance was sixty and square-shouldered, with the habit of putting the worst number first so that no one could accuse her of hiding it. She turned from the window to face the back of the room.

**Teodora Vance**  
Don't tell me it's talking. We have no way to know it is speaking at all, and you are asking fourteen thousand people to stay under a possible weapon on the strength of a pattern. If I'm wrong about the weapon we lose the ice and a year. If you're wrong we lose the ring.

**Illuminara**  
I won't tell you it's talking. I haven't seen enough to say so, and you would be right not to believe me if I did. I'd like your dock-clock traffic log, Dr. Brannock's flare record, the specifications of every detector, and the room until the evening session.

**Teodora Vance**  
The council sits at eighteen hundred. At eighteen hundred I put the evacuation to a vote.

**Illuminara**  
Then I'll bring you something you can test before you vote.
Vance looked at the clock and then at her. Curiosity did not soften her face; it made the responsibility in it more exact.

**Teodora Vance**  
Test it with what? We have sixty-nine hours and fifty-one minutes.

scenes.title: Nine Years of Margins
paragraphs: *Ring observatory, Brannock's office · Day 1, 09:30*

Ilse Brannock kept the flare record in a ledger as well as on the network, because the ledger could not be edited by anyone who disliked it. Nine years of the Wick filled it, night by night, in a small upright hand with questions in the margins. A few were underlined twice.

**Ilse Brannock**  
You're the ice woman with the thermal models.

**Illuminara**  
Today I'm the ice woman who read your flare record. It's very clean. Who keeps it?

**Ilse Brannock**  
I do. Nobody else wanted to. A flare is a flare.

**Illuminara**  
You don't think so.
Ilse put a hand flat on the ledger as one might on a sleeping animal.

**Ilse Brannock**  
I showed this to two people. One laughed, kindly, which was worse. I said the Wick grows louder when we do. After every busy evening the next burst is larger by about the same fraction. A star's flares don't care about our trade. I knew how it sounded, so I stopped saying it.

**Illuminara**  
And the timing?

**Ilse Brannock**  
Always in a gap. I called it the small hours because that was the gap we kept giving it.

Illuminara laid the traffic log over the flare record on the glass table. The observatory clock and dock clock were three minutes apart. Nobody had held the records together because the exchange net carried private trade.
She slid one trace by three minutes. The bright marks dropped into the troughs of the traffic like coins into a purse.

**Ilse Brannock**  
Four-oh-five. Shift change. The ring goes quiet for twenty minutes while the crews swap.

**Illuminara**  
The size follows the loudness before the gap. The timing follows the gap itself. If there is an intention here, the least extravagant account is not anger. It is turn-taking: something raising its voice over a crowd, then waiting not to be overwritten. But the same trace could still come from a rotating spot, a precursor that suppresses our band, or chance.

**Ilse Brannock**  
Say what you want to do.

**Illuminara**  
Move the gap. Fill four-oh-five with ordinary traffic, open a new gap at seven, and write every prediction before we touch the switches.

**Ilse Brannock**  
The exchange monitor shares the band. A precursor could fool it.

**Illuminara**  
What does not share it?

**Ilse Brannock**  
The old bolometric plate. Hard wire, separate clock, nothing in the exchange band. Rourke wanted it scrapped.

**Illuminara**  
Then it stays. And you present the test. I will not borrow nine years of your listening and call it my discovery.
Ilse looked at the double-underlined question in her ledger. *Hope is not evidence,* Illuminara thought. *But shame can hide evidence for years if nobody makes room for the person carrying it.*

Illuminara turned the ledger's pages back to the worst flares and forward to the Day Four forecast, and stopped. The test would tell them whether the star kept time. It would not shrink the burst already coming.

**Illuminara**  
One more thing, and it is a question about your own margins. If the size follows the loudness before the gap, then the Day Four burst is not fixed. It is being sized right now by what we do on the evening of Day Three. What happens to the flare after a quiet evening?

Ilse turned eight pages without looking for them. The smallest flares in the book were all there: the nights after the ring had gone dark for the harvest festival, when the trade band was nearly empty by dusk.

**Ilse Brannock**  
Small. They're the smallest in the book. I put them down to the calendar.

**Illuminara**  
Then the lever is the dusk peak, not the gap. If the council can cap one evening's traffic before the Day Four alignment, the parasol may meet something near eight-tenths instead of one point three. Pell will have to model it. I can't promise it. I can tell you which number to try to move.

**Ilse Brannock**  
I will present it if the envelope contains the ways I may be wrong.

**Illuminara**  
Put them first.

scenes.title: The Case for Flight
paragraphs: *Council chamber · Day 1, 18:00*

Vance opened the session by reading the clock aloud: fifty-eight hours, ten minutes. Then she gave the floor to Rourke, who stood with his hands behind him, like a man giving evidence in a trial he hoped to lose.

**Pell Rourke**  
The dangerous dawn alignment on Day Four, ordinary traffic, one point three of rating. Our two requested test gaps may draw smaller responses before it. If they do, that is new behavior, not the seventh and eighth members of the old sequence. It may strengthen the case for turn-taking, or mean the experiment itself is increasing the hazard.

**Teodora Vance**  
That's the case for flight, and I will make it myself so nobody thinks I haven't. Evacuations fail when they start late. A star that changes because we ask it to is not automatically safer than a star that does not.
Gideon Farrow rose from the guild benches. He was round and beautifully dressed and had been counting something in his head for the whole session.

**Gideon Farrow**  
Who pays if we flee from a weather event? The ice is my guild's wages and the ring's drinking water. It can't be that nobody may ask whether the star is just a star.

**Teodora Vance**  
Nobody has forbidden it. Dr. Brannock?
Ilse stood. Her hands were steady on the lectern, and Illuminara, three rows back, saw her find the notes she had meant not to need.

**Ilse Brannock**  
I have nine years of flares, three instruments and three clocks. The timing sits in the quiet of our traffic, and the size follows the loudness before it. I have three rivals: a spot rotating every twenty-four-point-one hours, a lull caused by a precursor rather than chosen by us, and chance.

**Teodora Vance**  
How much chance?

**Ilse Brannock**  
I kept the clustering and the one-a-month background of the nine-year record, and shuffled ten thousand pairs of gaps with the same widths and traffic levels. Seven pairs caught bursts in both timing windows and both amplitude bands. Seven in ten thousand is not zero. It is also not an argument I would throw away.

**Dov Achterberg**  
A calculation built from the same ledger that suggested the question. And your windows are fifty minutes wide.

**Ilse Brannock**  
Yes. Which is why the spot and precursor predictions are sealed beside ours. If the spot fires at the old hour, we lose. If the exchange band fails while the independent plate stays quiet, we lose. If one requested result misses, we write miss before we explain anything.

**Illuminara**  
At four-oh-five tomorrow we fill the usual gap with ordinary traffic. At seven we pause the exchange net for twenty-two minutes. The independent plate remains live. We repeat with a shorter gap after the next dusk peak. And there is a second lever, which the ledger itself points to. The size follows the loudness before the gap, so the Day Four burst is being sized by the evening of Day Three. If the guild caps that one dusk peak, Pell's median should fall well below the parasol's rating. That is a prediction too, and it can fail. The council writes the stop conditions.

**Gideon Farrow**  
What does the pause cost my traders? And what does your cap cost them?

**Illuminara**  
Tell the room what they need to keep.

**Gideon Farrow**  
The settlement hour. Move around it and I will sell the test to the guild. The cap I will price tonight, and the number will not be small: that dusk is my best evening of the quarter. I won't sell a permanent blackout, and I won't sell a permanent cap.

**Dov Achterberg**  
Nor should he. A scheduled silence is a scheduled vulnerability. Medical calls, collision alarms, smugglers who know when nobody is looking. If the proposed cure requires fourteen thousand people to become deaf on a timetable, I prefer the ferries.
Illuminara turned toward him rather than back to the lectern.

**Illuminara**  
Then the test must preserve an emergency carrier outside the crowded band, and any lasting arrangement must be movable. Nadim, can that be done without contaminating the plate?

**Nadim Oyelaran**  
A narrow red channel, hard-limited to alarms and medical speech. The plate won't see it. For a lasting window, the Chair could choose within a ninety-minute band and announce it fifteen minutes ahead.

**Teodora Vance**  
Noted. My cancel line: any requested burst over nine-tenths, any burst outside both registered windows, any failure of the independent plate, or any failure of the red channel. The ferries are fuelled tonight and manifests cut. A trigger starts loading within one hour; completing it still takes twenty-six. Nobody edits that sentence afterward.

scenes.title: The Gap Moves
paragraphs: *Communications office, exchange net · Day 2, 06:52*

At four-oh-five the old gap had been filled, and the Wick had said nothing. The exchange band stayed clean; so did the independent bolometric plate. Ilse had been awake since the previous morning and sat very straight in a chair she had not chosen.

**Nadim Oyelaran**  
Sealed envelope is in the council log. Rotation said four-oh-five, which did not happen. Precursor said the exchange band would fail there while the plate remained quiet, which did not happen. Turn-taking says seven, within twenty-five minutes, between half and seven-tenths of rating.

The pause had been posted in the council log the evening before, so that every office would know to expect it. At seven the exchange net went quiet. Kitchens went on, ferries stayed fuelled, and the red emergency carrier whispered with two medical calls and one collision alarm. The trading floor stopped for twenty-two minutes as fourteen thousand people agreed to leave a space.

The hard-wired plate drew a flat line, then a flat line, and then a sharp stroke at seven-oh-two. The network monitor followed a fraction later. The long shoulder on the decay was the mark Ilse had drawn in her ledger for nine years.

**Ilse Brannock**  
Fifty-eight hundredths on the plate.

**Nadim Oyelaran**  
Inside timing and amplitude. Red channel never dropped.
Nobody cheered. Illuminara held Ilse's elbow only after the older woman reached for her.

**Ilse Brannock**  
One.

**Illuminara**  
One.

At seven-oh-six a cargo tug on the outer rail killed its transponder and began drifting toward the customs lock. Dov's security desk saw it only because the lock's alarm line rode the red carrier, and the desk had four minutes to seal the lock before the tug's crew reached it.

**Dov Achterberg**  
Lock six sealed. Tug has gone back to its berth. They knew our hour because we posted our hour.
He said it to the room, not to Illuminara, and he did not say *I told you.* The tug's name went into the log beside the minutes.

The second requested gap came at twenty-two thirty on the same day, after a smaller dusk peak than the evening before: a stalled ferry queue the guild had not planned. A weak rise appeared on the exchange monitor eleven minutes before the pause. Dov, watching from the council feed, called it a precursor. The hard-wired plate stayed level.
At twenty-two thirty-six the Wick flared. The registered amplitude band ended at forty hundredths. The plate climbed to forty-one.

**Dov Achterberg**  
Outside the envelope.

**Ilse Brannock**  
By one hundredth. It is a miss.

**Nadim Oyelaran**  
The early rise was our own carrier leaking into the exchange monitor. It is absent from the plate. That defeats the precursor claim, but it does not put the amplitude back inside the envelope.

**Pell Rourke**  
And two requested responses in sixteen hours are faster than even the forty-four-hour cluster we started with. If we are causing them, that matters more than whether we have taught the sun manners.

Illuminara studied the two traces and did not rescue her prediction. Beside the second trace Ilse had written the evening's peak, and beside the first, the evening before. She set the two numbers side by side and left them without comment.

**Ilse Brannock**  
Fifty-eight hundredths after the loud evening. Forty-one after the quiet one.

**Pell Rourke**  
One pair.

**Ilse Brannock**  
One pair. It fell the right way. It is not a law, and I will not write it as one.

**Illuminara**  
Record the timing hit, the amplitude miss, the failed precursor rival, the faster cadence and the pair of evenings. Then stop opening gaps until the council decides what the faster cadence means.

**Ilse Brannock**  
You wanted a second night.

**Illuminara**  
I wanted an answer that could tell us no. This one has.

scenes.title: Forty Hours
paragraphs: *Council chamber · Day 2, 23:10*

Clock hour forty-one found the chamber full, with twenty-nine hours left on the wall and one hour before the order would have to go out. Under the clock were four lines, none softened: OLD-GAP SILENCE; FIRST REQUEST HIT; SECOND REQUEST TIMING HIT / AMPLITUDE MISS; REQUESTED CADENCE FASTER THAN BACKGROUND.

**Teodora Vance**  
Nobody in this room gets to call that two clean predictions. Dr. Brannock, what survives?

**Ilse Brannock**  
The rotating-spot prediction failed at four-oh-five. The precursor prediction failed on the independent plate. In ten thousand paired shuffles, seven matched both timing and amplitude; ours matched both timings but only one amplitude. The data still prefers schedule-response. It does not prove a mind, and the faster cadence may be a cost of asking.

**Dov Achterberg**  
Then stop asking and load the ferries. The experiment changed the thing we feared. And it told every smuggler on the outer rail what hour to move.

**Pell Rourke**  
Or exposed that it was already waiting for gaps we happened to give it. The Day Four burst remains the dangerous one. Capping the Day Three dusk peak alone takes my median from one point three to about one point zero. Turning the parasol before dawn takes it to about nine-tenths. What the bounded silence adds I cannot separate from the rest, and I will not pretend to. Together, eight-tenths.

**Dov Achterberg**  
Median. Your upper edge?

**Pell Rourke**  
Nine-tenths. At the cancel line.
The two numbers stayed between them. Vance looked not at Illuminara but at Ilse.

**Teodora Vance**  
If we stay, what do you ask the Wick to do?

**Ilse Brannock**  
Nothing beyond what the dangerous burst may do anyway. One bounded silence at dawn, three pulses from our cutter, then no second request. If the flare comes in the window and under the line, we learn whether leaving room changes the load. If not, the manifests are already cut.

**Gideon Farrow**  
The cap costs the guild its best settlement of the quarter, on the Day Three dusk. We will take it once. Not daily, and not without the loss entered beside the science.

**Dov Achterberg**  
And the notice. The tug at lock six knew seven o'clock because we gave it thirteen hours. No fixed daily blackout, and no posted hour. The Chair chooses inside a ninety-minute band and announces it fifteen minutes ahead. The red channel stays open. Security may cancel without your permission. And the tug is mine to answer for, not the science's.

**Nadim Oyelaran**  
I can enforce that in hardware. Trade carrier dark; red carrier live; plate independent. Six signatures to change it.

Illuminara had come in with a posted window and was leaving with a hidden one. She wrote Dov's clause into the draft protocol in his own words, and when he read it over her shoulder he changed one verb back.

**Teodora Vance**  
The ferries stay fuelled. Loading starts within one hour if the plate crosses nine-tenths, the flare leaves the window, the red carrier fails, or security calls the silence unsafe. Anyone may take a berth now. We attempt one bounded exchange at dawn. Dov's moving-window amendment and Farrow's cost ledger are part of the motion.
The vote passed seven to four, not nine to two. Dov voted no. His amendment passed eleven to zero.
Afterward the reply was designed in the communications office. Nadim had the forty-metre ice-cutting array. Ilse had her ledger open to the rising edge of the first requested flare.

**Nadim Oyelaran**  
I can give it a beam. I can't tell you it will see it.

**Ilse Brannock**  
Three pulses on the rhythm of its own rise. Then silence for as long as the pulses took. Heard, and your turn.

**Illuminara**  
No claim about what it means.

**Ilse Brannock**  
No. Only a courtesy we can withdraw.

scenes.title: A Turn at Four-Oh-Five
paragraphs: *Calloway Reach, communications office and Rakel Quay · Day 4, 04:05*

Under ordinary traffic the dangerous burst had been forecast at one point three of parasol rating. On the evening of Day Three the guild had capped its dusk peak, and Farrow's ledger carried the loss: the best evening of the quarter. Turning the parasol cost a month's thruster propellant and left Rakel Quay outside its full shadow. Rourke's registered range was seven-tenths to nine-tenths. Nine-tenths remained the line.

The Chair chose four-oh-five from the ninety-minute band and announced it fifteen minutes before. The red carrier stayed live. In the communications office Nadim held the beam trigger. On Rakel Quay his sister Kemi and two riggers waited beside the relay-mast breakers, because the model said the exposed masts would take the first side-load.

**Kemi Oyelaran**  
Rakel ready. You owe me two masts if your polite sun sneezes.

**Nadim Oyelaran**  
Put them on Farrow's ledger.

**Gideon Farrow**  
They are already there.

At four-oh-five Nadim sent three pulses. The trade band remained silent afterward. A medical call crossed the red carrier from nursery six; a child had swallowed a button. The silence did not make the ring helpless.
Four minutes passed.
The independent plate climbed.

**Pell Rourke**  
Point six. Point seven-two. Parasol taking thirty-one percent.
A second shoulder rose under the first.

**Teodora Vance**  
Read the plate, not the model.

**Pell Rourke**  
Point eight-six.

At Rakel, the first mast began to arc. Kemi cut its breaker before the automatic relay understood what was happening. The mast folded across an empty loading rail. The second leaned toward a fuel line.

**Kemi Oyelaran**  
Losing west two. Clearing the line now.
She drove the quay tug into the mast's lower brace. Metal went down away from the fuel line, taking the tug's manipulator arm with it.

**Nadim Oyelaran**  
Kemi?

**Kemi Oyelaran**  
Still expensive.
The plate touched eighty-nine hundredths. For twelve seconds its uncertainty band crossed the line, though the central reading did not.

**Teodora Vance**  
Rourke.

**Pell Rourke**  
Central reading below nine. Structure stable. My recommendation is hold, Chair. Your line says over, not near.
Vance's finger rested on the loading order. She could have called uncertainty a trigger. Nobody would have blamed her.

**Teodora Vance**  
Hold. Kemi has the quay. Red carrier is live. If the central plate rises one hundredth, load.
It did not. The long shoulder fell through eight-tenths, then seven. The parasol held. Rakel lost two relay masts and one tug arm; no one was hurt.
In the decay, with Nadim's array still silent and the ring keeping the space it had promised, the independent plate drew three small steps.

**Ilse Brannock**  
Three. I have nine years and it has never made three.

**Illuminara**  
Don't read it yet. We don't know that it's a reply.

**Ilse Brannock**  
No. We know only that it happened after our three.

They did not repeat the request that night. The next day the council authorized one movable window, with the red channel and security veto intact, and required a fresh vote every seven days. Dov's desk added a standing check of the outer rail to every window, a duty the protocol still carries under his name. Farrow entered the lost settlement, two masts, a tug arm and a month of propellant in the same ledger as the avoided evacuation. Dov signed the safety protocol and wrote beneath his name that he still believed they should leave.

**Teodora Vance**  
He is allowed to be wrong in the record, if he is wrong.

**Illuminara**  
So are we.
Ilse closed her ledger, opened it again, and wrote on the next clean line in her small upright hand: *Four-oh-five. We stopped. It knocked.*

critic_line: A frightened ring learns to answer an uncertain star without pretending certainty: Illuminara turns a dismissed ledger, a dissenter's real security warning and a guild's named sacrifice into a bounded test that saves fourteen thousand people while preserving everyone's right to remain unconvinced.

literary_score.method: Exact 50/50 mean of two independent READER_APPEAL_R1 reader judgments
shared_strengths: Dialogue-heavy, humane, idea-driven first-contact story with a rigorous, falsifiable test, honest misses, and costs recorded. Strong ending (three steps; 'It knocked'). Dense numbers and procedural council debate may slow some readers; characters are lightly differentiated and tension is managed rather than visceral.

A tense, humane first-contact problem unfolds through credible argument, testable uncertainty, and consequential compromise. The procedural density may tire some readers, but the distinctive turn-taking idea, principled dissent, escalating experiment, and superb final line make the story unusually gripping and memorable.
shared_reservations: Reader attention was most at risk around: “Four-oh-five. Shift change. The ring goes quiet for twenty minutes while the crews swap.”

Reader attention was most at risk around: “I kept the clustering and the one-a-month background of the nine-year record, and shuffled ten thousand pairs of gaps with the same widths and traffic levels.”

translation_sl.title: ZVEZDA, KI JE GOVORILA SAMO Z IZBRUHI
translation_sl.deck: Obročasti habitat s štirinajst tisoč prebivalci ima sedemdeset ur, da se odloči, ali ga njegova zvezda napada, edini dokaz, da ga ne, pa je tišina, ki je ni še nihče pomislil izmeriti.
translation_sl.shape: Šest prizorov v štirih dneh: svetov argument za beg, devetletni dnevnik fizičarke in vzvod, skrit v njem, glasovanje pod pogoji, ki jih je napisal svet, dve premaknjeni vrzeli brez čistega odgovora, odločitev, ki jo spremenijo njeni nasprotniki, in zora, ko ves obroč utihne, zvezda pa odgovori v obliki, ki je še nihče ne zna brati.

scenes.title: Sedemdeset ur
paragraphs: *Calloway Reach, dvorana sveta obroča · 1. dan, 06:10*

Ura na steni dvorane je kazala 70:00:00. Nekdo jo je postavil tja zato, da bi čas izgovorili naglas, pa ga ni nihče. Zunaj dolgega okna se je obroč počasi vrtel pod rdečo zvezdo, veliko kakor kovanec, na njegovi notranji strani je živelo štirinajst tisoč ljudi, v prostoru pa je dišalo po hladnem čaju in svetu, ki ni spal.

Illuminara je tri tedne prej prispela na krovu lednega tenderja; zadruga Rakel jo je najela, da modelira, kako toplota in svetloba obremenjujeta rezalne pomole. V dvorani je bila, ker so bili njeni modeli edini, s katerimi se še nihče ni prepiral. Stala je zadaj ob vrču z vodo.

**Teodora Vance**  
Wick je v enajstih dneh sprožil šest nevarnih izbruhov. V devetih letih zapisov je sprožil približno enega na mesec. Enajst dni je dvesto štiriinšestdeset ur; šest izbruhov v tem času pomeni enega na štiriinštirideset ur, tega pa ne morem spraviti med nihanja ozadja. Kopičijo se po naših večernih prometnih konicah. Naslednja naravna poravnava se pričakuje okoli štirih zjutraj četrtega dne. Ob običajnem prometu urad za ščit napoveduje eno celo tri nazivne zmogljivosti našega senčnika. Trajekti potrebujejo šestindvajset ur, da končajo natovarjanje, jaz pa iz življenj na obroču ne bom izrezala dvourne rezerve. Ukaz mora biti izdan do dvainštiridesete ure.

**Pell Rourke**  
Senčnik prenese en izbruh. Ne bom obljubil, da prenese tistega.

**Illuminara**  
Kaj stane odhod?

**Teodora Vance**  
Rakel. Vse, kar rudarimo. Obroč, ki odide, s seboj odnese osem mesecev vode, potem pa postane zelo velik kozarec.

Vance je bila stara šestdeset let in širokih ramen, navado pa je imela najprej povedati najslabše število, da ji nihče ne bi mogel očitati prikrivanja. Od okna se je obrnila proti zadnjemu delu prostora.

**Teodora Vance**  
Ne govorite mi, da govori. Nikakor ne moremo vedeti, ali sploh govori, vi pa od štirinajst tisoč ljudi zahtevate, naj ostanejo pod morebitnim orožjem na podlagi vzorca. Če se jaz motim glede orožja, izgubimo led in leto dni. Če se motite vi, izgubimo obroč.

**Illuminara**  
Ne bom vam govorila, da govori. Nisem videla dovolj, da bi to trdila, in prav bi imeli, če mi ne bi verjeli. Potrebujem vaš dnevnik prometa po pristaniški uri, dnevnik izbruhov doktorice Brannock, specifikacije vseh detektorjev in ta prostor do večerne seje.

**Teodora Vance**  
Svet zaseda ob osemnajstih. Ob osemnajstih dam evakuacijo na glasovanje.

**Illuminara**  
Potem vam bom pred glasovanjem prinesla nekaj, kar lahko preizkusite.
Vance je pogledala uro in nato njo. Radovednost ji ni omehčala obraza; odgovornost na njem je naredila natančnejšo.

**Teodora Vance**  
S čim boste to preizkusili? Imamo devetinšestdeset ur in enainpetdeset minut.

scenes.title: Devet let robnih zapiskov
paragraphs: *Observatorij obroča, pisarna Brannockove · 1. dan, 09:30*

Ilse Brannock je dnevnik izbruhov vodila v knjigi in na omrežju, ker knjige ni mogel urejati nihče, ki mu vsebina ni bila všeč. Devet let Wicka jo je polnilo noč za nočjo, z drobno pokončno pisavo in vprašanji ob robovih. Nekaj jih je bilo dvakrat podčrtanih.

**Ilse Brannock**  
Vi ste ženska za led s toplotnimi modeli.

**Illuminara**  
Danes sem ženska za led, ki je prebrala vaš dnevnik izbruhov. Zelo čist je. Kdo ga vodi?

**Ilse Brannock**  
Jaz. Nihče drug ga ni hotel. Izbruh je pač izbruh.

**Illuminara**  
Vi ne mislite tako.
Ilse je položila dlan na knjigo, kakor bi jo položila na spečo žival.

**Ilse Brannock**  
To sem pokazala dvema človekoma. Eden se je zasmejal, prijazno, kar je bilo še huje. Rekla sem, da Wick postane glasnejši, ko postanemo glasnejši mi. Po vsakem prometnem večeru je naslednji izbruh večji za približno enak delež. Zvezdini izbruhi se ne menijo za našo trgovino. Vedela sem, kako zveni, zato sem o tem nehala govoriti.

**Illuminara**  
Kaj pa čas?

**Ilse Brannock**  
Vedno v vrzeli. Rekla sem ji zgodnje ure, ker smo ji takrat vedno dajali vrzel.

Illuminara je dnevnik prometa položila čez dnevnik izbruhov na stekleni mizi. Ura observatorija in pristaniška ura sta se razlikovali za tri minute. Nihče zapisov ni držal skupaj, ker je borzno omrežje prenašalo zasebne posle.
Eno sled je premaknila za tri minute. Svetle oznake so padle v doline prometa kakor kovanci v mošnjo.

**Ilse Brannock**  
Štiri nič pet. Menjava izmene. Obroč za dvajset minut utihne, medtem ko se ekipe zamenjajo.

**Illuminara**  
Velikost sledi glasnosti pred vrzeljo. Čas sledi sami vrzeli. Če je tukaj namen, najmanj pretirana razlaga ni jeza. Je izmenjava besede: nekaj dvigne glas nad množico in nato čaka, da ga ne prepišemo. Toda enako sled bi še vedno lahko povzročili vrteča se pega, predhodni pojav, ki zatre naš pas, ali naključje.

**Ilse Brannock**  
Povejte, kaj želite narediti.

**Illuminara**  
Premakniti vrzel. Štiri nič pet zapolniti z običajnim prometom, odpreti novo vrzel ob sedmih in vsako napoved zapisati, preden se dotaknemo stikal.

**Ilse Brannock**  
Nadzornik borze uporablja isti pas. Predhodni pojav bi ga lahko prevaral.

**Illuminara**  
Kaj ga ne uporablja?

**Ilse Brannock**  
Stara bolometrična plošča. Žična povezava, ločena ura, nič v borznem pasu. Rourke jo je hotel zavreči.

**Illuminara**  
Potem ostane. Preizkus pa predstavite vi. Ne bom si izposodila devetih let vašega poslušanja in temu rekla svoje odkritje.
Ilse je pogledala dvakrat podčrtano vprašanje v svojem dnevniku. *Upanje ni dokaz,* je pomislila Illuminara. *Toda sram lahko leta skriva dokaz, če nihče ne naredi prostora človeku, ki ga nosi.*

Illuminara je obrnila strani dnevnika nazaj k najhujšim izbruhom in naprej k napovedi za četrti dan ter se ustavila. Preizkus bi jim povedal, ali zvezda sledi času. Ne bi zmanjšal izbruha, ki je že prihajal.

**Illuminara**  
Še nekaj, in to je vprašanje o vaših robnih zapiskih. Če velikost sledi glasnosti pred vrzeljo, izbruh četrtega dne ni določen. Prav zdaj mu velikost daje to, kar počnemo tretji dan zvečer. Kaj se zgodi z izbruhom po tihem večeru?
Ilse je obrnila osem strani, ne da bi jih iskala. Najmanjši izbruhi v knjigi so bili vsi tam: noči po prazniku žetve, ko je obroč potemnel in je bil trgovski pas do mraka skoraj prazen.

**Ilse Brannock**  
Majhni. Najmanjši v knjigi so. Pripisala sem jih koledarju.

**Illuminara**  
Potem je vzvod večerna konica, ne vrzel. Če lahko svet omeji promet enega večera pred poravnavo četrtega dne, bo senčnik morda dobil nekaj blizu osmih desetin namesto ena cele tri. Pell bo to moral modelirati. Tega ne morem obljubiti. Lahko vam povem, katero številko naj poskusite premakniti.

**Ilse Brannock**  
Predstavila bom, če bodo v ovojnici načini, kako se lahko motim.

**Illuminara**  
Postavite jih na prvo mesto.

scenes.title: Argument za beg
paragraphs: *Dvorana sveta · 1. dan, 18:00*

Vance je sejo začela tako, da je na glas prebrala uro: oseminpetdeset ur in deset minut. Nato je dala besedo Rourku, ki je stal z rokami za hrbtom kakor človek, ki pričuje na sojenju, za katero upa, da ga bo izgubil.

**Pell Rourke**  
Nevarna poravnava ob zori četrtega dne, običajen promet, ena cela tri nazivne zmogljivosti. Naši dve zahtevani preizkusni vrzeli lahko pred tem prikličeta manjša odziva. Če ju, bo to novo vedenje, ne sedmi in osmi člen starega zaporedja. Lahko okrepi razlago o izmenjavi besede ali pa pomeni, da poskus sam povečuje nevarnost.

**Teodora Vance**  
To je argument za beg in povedala ga bom sama, da nihče ne bo mislil, da ga nisem upoštevala. Evakuacije propadejo, ko se začnejo prepozno. Zvezda, ki se spremeni, ker jo prosimo, ni samodejno varnejša od zvezde, ki se ne.
Gideon Farrow je vstal s klopi ceha. Bil je okrogel, brezhibno oblečen in vso sejo je nekaj štel v glavi.

**Gideon Farrow**  
Kdo plača, če zbežimo pred vremenskim pojavom? Led je plača mojega ceha in pitna voda obroča. Ne more veljati, da nihče ne sme vprašati, ali je zvezda samo zvezda.

**Teodora Vance**  
Nihče tega ni prepovedal. Doktorica Brannock?
Ilse je vstala. Roke na govorniškem pultu so bile mirne, Illuminara pa jo je tri vrste zadaj videla najti zapiske, za katere je nameravala, da jih ne bo potrebovala.

**Ilse Brannock**  
Imam devet let izbruhov, tri instrumente in tri ure. Čas leži v tišini našega prometa, velikost pa sledi glasnosti pred njo. Imam tri tekmece: pego, ki se vrti vsakih štiriindvajset celih ena ura, zatišje, ki ga povzroča predhodni pojav in ne mi, ter naključje.

**Teodora Vance**  
Koliko naključja?

**Ilse Brannock**  
Ohranila sem kopičenje in ozadje enega izbruha na mesec iz devetletnega dnevnika ter deset tisočkrat premešala pare vrzeli z enakimi širinami in ravnmi prometa. Sedem parov je ujelo izbruhe v obeh časovnih oknih in obeh pasovih amplitude. Sedem od deset tisoč ni nič. Prav tako ni argument, ki bi ga zavrgla.

**Dov Achterberg**  
Izračun, zgrajen iz istega dnevnika, ki je nakazal vprašanje. In vaša okna so široka petdeset minut.

**Ilse Brannock**  
Da. Zato so napovedi pege in predhodnega pojava zapečatene poleg naših. Če pega sproži ob stari uri, izgubimo. Če borzni pas odpove, medtem ko je neodvisna plošča tiha, izgubimo. Če en zahtevani rezultat zgreši, napišemo zgrešeno, preden kar koli razlagamo.

**Illuminara**  
Jutri ob štiri nič pet zapolnimo običajno vrzel z običajnim prometom. Ob sedmih za dvaindvajset minut ustavimo borzno omrežje. Neodvisna plošča ostane vključena. Po naslednji večerni konici ponovimo s krajšo vrzeljo. Obstaja še drugi vzvod, na katerega kaže sam dnevnik. Velikost sledi glasnosti pred vrzeljo, zato izbruhu četrtega dne velikost daje večer tretjega dne. Če ceh omeji tisto eno konico ob mraku, bi morala Pellova mediana pasti precej pod nazivno zmogljivost senčnika. Tudi to je napoved in tudi ta lahko spodleti. Svet napiše pogoje za prekinitev.

**Gideon Farrow**  
Kaj premor stane moje trgovce? In kaj jih stane vaša omejitev?

**Illuminara**  
Povejte prostoru, kaj morajo ohraniti.

**Gideon Farrow**  
Uro poravnave poslov. Premaknite se okoli nje in preizkus bom prodal cehu. Omejitev bom ovrednotil nocoj in številka ne bo majhna: tisti mrak je moj najboljši večer četrtletja. Ne bom prodal trajnega izklopa in ne bom prodal trajne omejitve.

**Dov Achterberg**  
Pa tudi ne bi smeli. Načrtovana tišina je načrtovana ranljivost. Zdravniški klici, opozorila pred trki, tihotapci, ki vedo, kdaj nihče ne gleda. Če predlagano zdravilo zahteva, da štirinajst tisoč ljudi po urniku ogluši, imam raje trajekte.
Illuminara se je obrnila k njemu in ne nazaj h govorniškemu pultu.

**Illuminara**  
Potem mora preizkus ohraniti kanal za nujne primere zunaj zasedenega pasu, vsaka trajnejša ureditev pa mora biti premična. Nadim, je to mogoče brez onesnaženja plošče?

**Nadim Oyelaran**  
Ozek rdeči kanal, strojno omejen na alarme in zdravstvene pogovore. Plošča ga ne bo videla. Za trajno okno lahko predsednica izbere čas znotraj devetdesetminutnega pasu in ga napove petnajst minut prej.

**Teodora Vance**  
Zapisano. Moja meja za prekinitev: vsak zahtevani izbruh nad devetimi desetinami, vsak izbruh zunaj obeh registriranih oken, vsaka odpoved neodvisne plošče ali vsaka odpoved rdečega kanala. Trajekti bodo nocoj napolnjeni z gorivom in seznami potnikov sestavljeni. Sprožilec začne natovarjanje v eni uri; dokončanje še vedno traja šestindvajset. Tega stavka pozneje nihče ne popravlja.

scenes.title: Vrzel se premakne
paragraphs: *Komunikacijski urad, borzno omrežje · 2. dan, 06:52*

Ob štiri nič pet so staro vrzel zapolnili in Wick ni rekel ničesar. Borzni pas je ostal čist; prav tako neodvisna bolometrična plošča. Ilse je bila budna od prejšnjega jutra in je sedela zelo vzravnano na stolu, ki ga ni izbrala.

**Nadim Oyelaran**  
Zapečatena ovojnica je v zapisniku sveta. Vrtenje je napovedalo štiri nič pet, kar se ni zgodilo. Predhodni pojav je napovedal, da bo tam borzni pas odpovedal, plošča pa bo ostala tiha, kar se ni zgodilo. Izmenjava besede napoveduje sedmo uro, znotraj petindvajsetih minut, med polovico in sedmimi desetinami nazivne zmogljivosti.

Premor je bil prejšnji večer objavljen v zapisniku sveta, da bi ga pričakoval vsak urad. Ob sedmih je borzno omrežje utihnilo. Kuhinje so delovale, trajekti so ostali napolnjeni z gorivom, rdeči kanal za nujne primere pa je šepetal z dvema zdravstvenima klicema in enim opozorilom pred trkom. Trgovsko nadstropje se je ustavilo za dvaindvajset minut, ko se je štirinajst tisoč ljudi strinjalo, da pustijo prostor.

Žično povezana plošča je risala ravno črto, nato še eno ravno črto, nato pa oster poteg ob sedmih in dveh minutah. Omrežni nadzornik mu je sledil delček sekunde pozneje. Dolga rama pojemanja je bila znamenje, ki ga je Ilse devet let risala v svoj dnevnik.

**Ilse Brannock**  
Oseminpetdeset stotink na plošči.

**Nadim Oyelaran**  
Znotraj časa in amplitude. Rdeči kanal ni nikoli izpadel.
Nihče ni vzkliknil. Illuminara je prijela Ilse za komolec šele potem, ko je starejša ženska segla k njej.

**Ilse Brannock**  
Ena.

**Illuminara**  
Ena.

Ob sedmih in šest minut je tovorni vlačilec na zunanji tirnici ugasnil svoj oddajnik in začel drseti proti carinski zapornici. Dovova varnostna služba ga je opazila samo zato, ker je alarm zapornice potoval po rdečem kanalu, služba pa je imela štiri minute, da zapornico zapečati, preden jo je dosegla posadka vlačilca.

**Dov Achterberg**  
Zapornica šest je zapečatena. Vlačilec se je vrnil na privez. Našo uro so poznali, ker smo jo objavili.
To je povedal prostoru, ne Illuminari, in ni rekel *saj sem vam povedal*. Ime vlačilca je šlo v zapisnik poleg minut.

Druga zahtevana vrzel je prišla istega dne ob dvaindvajsetih trideset, po manjši večerni konici od prejšnjega večera: zastoj trajektov, ki ga ceh ni načrtoval. Enajst minut pred premorom se je na borznem nadzorniku pokazal šibek dvig. Dov, ki je gledal prenos sveta, ga je razglasil za predhodni pojav. Žično povezana plošča je ostala ravna.
Ob dvaindvajsetih šestintrideset je Wick izbruhnil. Registrirani pas amplitude se je končal pri štiridesetih stotinkah. Plošča se je dvignila na enainštirideset.

**Dov Achterberg**  
Zunaj ovojnice.

**Ilse Brannock**  
Za eno stotinko. Zgrešeno je.

**Nadim Oyelaran**  
Zgodnji dvig je bil naš nosilec, ki je uhajal v borzni nadzornik. Na plošči ga ni. To zavrne trditev o predhodnem pojavu, amplitude pa ne spravi nazaj v ovojnico.

**Pell Rourke**  
Dva zahtevana odziva v šestnajstih urah sta tudi hitrejša od že tako zgoščene štiriinštirideseturne pogostosti, s katero smo začeli. Če ju povzročamo mi, je to pomembnejše od tega, ali smo sonce naučili manir.

Illuminara je preučila obe sledi in svoje napovedi ni reševala. Ob drugi sledi je Ilse zapisala večerno konico, ob prvi pa prejšnji večer. Številki je položila drugo ob drugo in ju pustila brez komentarja.

**Ilse Brannock**  
Oseminpetdeset stotink po glasnem večeru. Enainštirideset po tihem.

**Pell Rourke**  
En par.

**Ilse Brannock**  
En par. Šel je v pravo smer. Ni zakon in kot zakon ga ne bom zapisala.

**Illuminara**  
Zapišite zadetek časa, zgrešeno amplitudo, zavrnjenega tekmeca s predhodnim pojavom, hitrejšo pogostost in par večerov. Nato ne odpirajte več vrzeli, dokler svet ne odloči, kaj hitrejša pogostost pomeni.

**Ilse Brannock**  
Želeli ste drugo noč.

**Illuminara**  
Želela sem odgovor, ki bi nam lahko rekel ne. Ta nam je.

scenes.title: Štirideset ur
paragraphs: *Dvorana sveta · 2. dan, 23:10*

Ob enainštirideseti uri je bila dvorana polna, na steni je ostalo devetindvajset ur, do časa, ko bi moral biti izdan ukaz, pa ena. Pod uro so stale štiri neomiljene vrstice: TIŠINA V STARI VRZELI; PRVA ZAHTEVA ZADETA; DRUGA ZAHTEVA ZADET ČAS / ZGREŠENA AMPLITUDA; ZAHTEVANA POGOSTOST HITREJŠA OD OZADJA.

**Teodora Vance**  
Nihče v tem prostoru tega ne sme imenovati dve čisti napovedi. Doktorica Brannock, kaj ostane?

**Ilse Brannock**  
Napoved vrteče se pege je ob štiri nič pet spodletela. Napoved predhodnega pojava je spodletela na neodvisni plošči. Pri deset tisoč premešanih parih se jih je sedem ujemalo v času in amplitudi; naša sta se ujemala v obeh časih, toda le v eni amplitudi. Podatki še vedno dajejo prednost odzivu na urnik. Ne dokazujejo uma, hitrejša pogostost pa je lahko cena spraševanja.

**Dov Achterberg**  
Potem nehajte spraševati in natovorite trajekte. Poskus je spremenil stvar, ki smo se je bali. Vsakemu tihotapcu na zunanji tirnici je tudi povedal, ob kateri uri naj se premakne.

**Pell Rourke**  
Ali pa je razkril, da je že čakala na vrzeli, ki smo ji jih po naključju dajali. Izbruh četrtega dne ostaja nevaren. Sama omejitev konice ob mraku tretjega dne zniža mojo mediano z ene cele tri na približno ena celo nič. Obrat senčnika pred zoro jo zniža na približno devet desetin. Kar doda omejena tišina, ne morem ločiti od preostalega in ne bom se pretvarjal, da lahko. Skupaj: osem desetin.

**Dov Achterberg**  
Mediana. Vaš zgornji rob?

**Pell Rourke**  
Devet desetin. Na meji za prekinitev.
Številki sta ostali med njima. Vance ni pogledala Illuminare, temveč Ilse.

**Teodora Vance**  
Če ostanemo, kaj prosite Wick, naj naredi?

**Ilse Brannock**  
Ničesar več od tega, kar bi nevarni izbruh morda naredil že tako. Ena omejena tišina ob zori, trije impulzi našega rezalnika, nato nobene druge zahteve. Če izbruh pride v oknu in pod mejo, izvemo, ali puščanje prostora spremeni obremenitev. Če ne, so seznami potnikov že sestavljeni.

**Gideon Farrow**  
Omejitev ceh stane najboljšo poravnavo poslov v četrtletju, ob mraku tretjega dne. Enkrat jo bomo sprejeli. Ne vsak dan in ne brez izgube, zapisane poleg znanosti.

**Dov Achterberg**  
In napoved. Vlačilec pri zapornici šest je vedel za sedmo uro, ker smo mu dali trinajst ur časa. Nobenega stalnega dnevnega izklopa in nobene objavljene ure. Predsednica izbere znotraj devetdesetminutnega pasu in jo napove petnajst minut prej. Rdeči kanal ostane odprt. Varnost lahko prekliče brez vašega dovoljenja. In za vlačilec odgovarjam jaz, ne znanost.

**Nadim Oyelaran**  
To lahko strojno uveljavim. Trgovski nosilec temen; rdeči nosilec živ; plošča neodvisna. Za spremembo je potrebnih šest podpisov.
Illuminara je vstopila z objavljenim oknom in odhajala s skritim. Dovovo določilo je v osnutek protokola zapisala z njegovimi besedami, on pa je med branjem čez njeno ramo en glagol spremenil nazaj.

**Teodora Vance**  
Trajekti ostanejo napolnjeni z gorivom. Natovarjanje se začne v eni uri, če plošča preseže devet desetin, če izbruh zapusti okno, če rdeči nosilec odpove ali če varnost razglasi tišino za nevarno. Kdor želi, lahko že zdaj zasede privez. Ob zori poskusimo eno omejeno izmenjavo. Dovov amandma o premičnem oknu in Farrowov dnevnik stroškov sta del predloga.
Glasovanje se je končalo s sedmimi glasovi proti štirim, ne z devetimi proti dvema. Dov je glasoval proti. Njegov amandma je bil sprejet z enajst proti nič.
Nato so v komunikacijskem uradu zasnovali odgovor. Nadim je imel štiridesetmetrsko polje za rezanje ledu. Ilse je imela dnevnik odprt pri naraščajočem robu prvega zahtevanega izbruha.

**Nadim Oyelaran**  
Lahko mu pošljem žarek. Ne morem vam povedati, da ga bo videlo.

**Ilse Brannock**  
Trije impulzi v ritmu njegovega naraščanja. Nato tišina, dolga toliko, kot so trajali impulzi. Slišano, zdaj si na vrsti.

**Illuminara**  
Brez trditve o tem, kaj pomeni.

**Ilse Brannock**  
Brez. Samo vljudnost, ki jo lahko umaknemo.

scenes.title: Beseda ob štiri nič pet
paragraphs: *Calloway Reach, komunikacijski urad in pomol Rakel · 4. dan, 04:05*

Ob običajnem prometu je bil nevarni izbruh napovedan pri eni celi tri nazivne zmogljivosti senčnika. Tretji dan zvečer je ceh omejil konico ob mraku, Farrowov dnevnik pa je nosil izgubo: najboljši večer četrtletja. Obračanje senčnika je stalo mesečno zalogo pogonskega goriva, pomol Rakel pa je ostal zunaj njegove polne sence. Rourkov registrirani razpon je bil od sedmih do devetih desetin. Devet desetin je ostalo meja.

Predsednica je iz devetdesetminutnega pasu izbrala štiri nič pet in čas napovedala petnajst minut prej. Rdeči nosilec je ostal živ. V komunikacijskem uradu je Nadim držal sprožilec žarka. Na pomolu Rakel so njegova sestra Kemi in dva monterja čakali ob odklopnikih relejnih jamborov, ker je model napovedal, da bodo izpostavljeni jambori prevzeli prvo stransko obremenitev.

**Kemi Oyelaran**  
Rakel pripravljen. Če vaše vljudno sonce kihne, mi dolgujete dva jambora.

**Nadim Oyelaran**  
Daj ju v Farrowov dnevnik.

**Gideon Farrow**  
Že sta v njem.

Ob štiri nič pet je Nadim poslal tri impulze. Trgovski pas je potem ostal tih. Po rdečem nosilcu je prišel zdravstveni klic iz jasli šest; otrok je pogoltnil gumb. Tišina obroča ni naredila nemočnega.
Minile so štiri minute.
Neodvisna plošča se je začela dvigati.

**Pell Rourke**  
Nič cela šest. Nič cela dvainsedemdeset. Senčnik prevzema enaintrideset odstotkov.
Pod prvim se je dvignila druga rama.

**Teodora Vance**  
Berite ploščo, ne modela.

**Pell Rourke**  
Nič cela šestinosemdeset.

Na Rakelu je prvi jambor začel obločno prebijati. Kemi je njegov odklopnik izključila, preden je samodejni rele razumel, kaj se dogaja. Jambor se je zložil čez prazno nakladalno tirnico. Drugi se je nagnil proti cevi za gorivo.

**Kemi Oyelaran**  
Izgubljamo zahodni dve. Zdaj čistim cev.
Pomolski vlačilec je zapeljala v spodnjo oporo jambora. Kovina je padla stran od cevi za gorivo in s seboj odnesla upravljalno roko vlačilca.

**Nadim Oyelaran**  
Kemi?

**Kemi Oyelaran**  
Še vedno drago.
Plošča se je dotaknila devetinosemdesetih stotink. Dvanajst sekund je njen pas negotovosti sekal mejo, čeprav je osrednji odčitek ni.

**Teodora Vance**  
Rourke.

**Pell Rourke**  
Osrednji odčitek pod devetimi desetinami. Struktura stabilna. Priporočam, da vztrajamo, predsednica. Vaša meja pravi nad, ne blizu.
Vance je držala prst na ukazu za natovarjanje. Negotovost bi lahko razglasila za sprožilec. Nihče ji ne bi očital.

**Teodora Vance**  
Vztrajamo. Kemi obvladuje pomol. Rdeči nosilec je živ. Če se osrednja plošča dvigne za eno stotinko, natovarjamo.
Ni se. Dolga rama je padla skozi osem desetin, nato sedem. Senčnik je zdržal. Rakel je izgubil dva relejna jambora in eno roko vlačilca; poškodovan ni bil nihče.
Med pojemanjem, ko je Nadimovo polje še molčalo in je obroč držal prostor, ki ga je obljubil, je neodvisna plošča narisala tri majhne stopnice.

**Ilse Brannock**  
Tri. Imam devet let in nikoli ni naredilo treh.

**Illuminara**  
Ne berite jih še. Ne vemo, ali je to odgovor.

**Ilse Brannock**  
Ne. Vemo le, da se je zgodilo po naših treh.

Tisto noč zahteve niso ponovili. Naslednji dan je svet odobril eno premično okno z ohranjenima rdečim kanalom in varnostnim vetom ter zahteval novo glasovanje vsakih sedem dni. Dovov urad je vsakemu oknu dodal stalni pregled zunanje tirnice, dolžnost, ki jo protokol še vedno nosi pod njegovim imenom. Farrow je izgubljeno poravnavo, dva jambora, roko vlačilca in mesečno zalogo goriva vpisal v isti dnevnik kot preprečeno evakuacijo. Dov je podpisal varnostni protokol in pod svojim imenom zapisal, da še vedno verjame, da bi morali oditi.

**Teodora Vance**  
V zapisu se sme motiti, če se moti.

**Illuminara**  
Tudi mi se smemo.
Ilse je zaprla dnevnik, ga znova odprla in v svoji drobni pokončni pisavi na naslednjo prazno vrstico zapisala: *Štiri nič pet. Ustavili smo se. Potrkalo je.*
